turns.prompt_text: I have an Adobe Illustrator file type. I would like to get the images and icons out of it.
turns.response_html:
The best method depends on whether or not you currently have Adobe Illustrator installed. Here are the workflows for both scenarios.

Scenario A: You have Adobe Illustrator

This is the most reliable way to maintain the quality of vector icons and the resolution of embedded images.

1. For Icons & Vector Graphics (The "Asset Export" Method)

This is the modern standard for batch-exporting multiple icons at once.

  • Open the file in Illustrator.
  • Go to Window > Asset Export to open the panel.
  • Select the icons or objects you want to extract on your artboard.
  • Drag and drop them into the Asset Export panel.
  • In the panel, select the format you want (use SVG for web/scalable vector icons, or PNG for standard transparent images).
  • Click Export.

2. For Embedded Photos (The "Unembed" Method)

If the file contains raster photos (JPEGs/PNGs) placed inside the design:

  • Select the image on the canvas.
  • Look at the Links panel (Window > Links).
  • Click the "hamburger" menu (three lines) in the top right of the Links panel.
  • Select Unembed. Illustrator will ask you where to save the standalone PSD or TIFF file, which you can then convert to JPG/PNG.

Scenario B: You do NOT have Adobe Illustrator

You can still extract assets using free tools or file-renaming tricks, as .ai files are often just PDF containers.

1. The PDF Rename Trick (Fastest)

Adobe Illustrator files are often saved with "PDF Compatibility."

  • Duplicate your .ai file (so you don't lose the original).
  • Right-click the copy and rename the file extension from .ai to .pdf.
  • Open this new PDF.
    • If you just need images: Use a free online tool like "PDF to JPG" or open it in Adobe Acrobat Pro and use "Export all Images."
    • If you need vector icons: Open the PDF in a free vector tool like Inkscape (see below).

2. Use Inkscape (Free Open Source Software)

Inkscape is a free alternative to Illustrator that can open .ai files.

  • Download and install Inkscape.
  • Open your .ai file in Inkscape.
  • Ungroup the elements (Ctrl + Shift + G) until individual icons are selectable.
  • Select an icon, go to File > Export, and choose "Selection" to export just that object as a PNG or SVG.

3. Online Conversion

If you can't install software, use a cloud converter.

  • Go to a site like CloudConvert or Zamzar.
  • Upload the .ai file.
  • To get icons: Convert to SVG or EPS.
  • To get images: Convert to PNG or JPG (Note: This flattens the whole image, so you will have to crop the icons out manually afterwards).

Summary of Formats

  • SVG: Best for icons. Infinite scalability, small file size, editable code.
  • PNG: Best for transparent images if SVG isn't supported.
  • JPG: Best for photos. No transparency.

Would you like me to explain the difference between vector (icons) and raster (photos) formats in more detail so you know which export setting to choose?
